subject: Phased activation + pooled commit proposal — GPU price trigger and rollback
messages:

Hi Rachel —

Thanks for the call yesterday. Our execs liked the performance numbers but they want a clearer path on how Redwood will protect Nebula from sudden GPU market spikes. Key asks: a) phased activation so we don't pay for idle capacity immediately, b) a price-trigger that allows partial rollback or credit if spot GPU index moves > 18% during the first 12 months, and c) a single-pane audit for usage.

I've attached our procurement RFI and a short workbook with expected QPS. Can you share a proposal that covers these three asks and any constraints on discounts? We need something to take into the exec meeting on Wed.

Best,
Asha
Procurement Lead — NebulaAI

Attachments: Nebula_Procurement_RFI.pdf, nebula_qps_workbook.csv

Date: 2026-08-09T11:03:00-07:00

Hi Asha —

Thanks for the clear asks and the workbook. Short answer: we can support phased activation + a price-trigger construct, but the discount/credit mechanics and the exact rollback language will need approval from finance and procurement on our side. I'm sending an internal note to loop in our pricing and legal owners.

High level proposal we can bake into the SOW this week:
- Phase 1: 25% of committed GPUs activated at signing; Phase 2: additional 50% activated at month 3; Phase 3: remaining 25% activated month 9 (can be pulled forward with 30-day notice).
- Price-trigger: if our GPU index (we use CloudVendor spot index) increases >18% vs baseline for a rolling 30-day window within first 12 months, Nebula is eligible for either a 6-month credit equal to the incremental per-token cost OR right to de-activate up to 30% of the inactive pool without penalty.
- Audit: token-level usage export and audit logs for 12 months; we can extend retention as an add-on.

I'll be explicit about the approval path in the next message and attach a draft SOW and a pricing matrix.

-Rachel
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Team —

Marking urgent. Asha's ask on the price-trigger will trigger a special approval for any credit/rollback we offer. Quick thoughts from pricing side:
- The phased activation is straightforward and preferred (reduces idle billing risk).
- The proposed 18% threshold is reasonable but the remedy needs to be one-way (credit or activation rights), not both. Risk: double comp.
- For Nebula size (they're targeting 1.2k A100-equivalent GPU-hrs/month initially), a 6-month credit could be material. We should model worst-case exposure (18% spike sustained for 30 days -> incremental cost), run it vs committed ARR.

Karthik / David — can you run a quick exposure calc and a recommended maximum credit cap (either $ or % of committed ARR) by EOD so Rachel can present a bounded ask to Nebula?

Monica
Head of Commercial Finance — Redwood Inference

Running the calc now — preliminary numbers:
- Baseline: $0.60 / GPU-hr (modeled) -> monthly infra cost ~ $720 (for per-GPU) * 1.2k GPUs? Note: need to confirm units with Nebula workbook; I'll validate the QPS->GPU map.
- If index spikes 18%: incremental ~ $0.108 / GPU-hr -> incremental monthly ~ $130k (ballpark) over the spike window.
- A 6-month credit at that incremental rate could be ~$780k; capped credits make sense.

Recommendation: offer a price-trigger remedy with a 12-month lookback, but cap the total credits at 15% of first-year committed spend. That keeps the remedy meaningful while protecting Redwood.

I'll share a quick spreadsheet to Monica and Rachel in 30.

-Karthik

Adding infra ops angle —

- The rollback (de-activate up to 30%) is doable if Nebula hasn't already consumed that pool; for de-activations that require re-scheduling other workloads, there may be a short operational lead time and we should specify a transition SLA (48-72 hours).
- For the price-trigger index, we must be explicit about the index provider (CloudVendor spot index) and the calculation method (30-day rolling avg).

Subject: RE: Phased activation + pooled commit proposal — GPU price trigger and rollback

Hi Asha —

Appreciate the quick turnaround on requirements. Attached is an updated one-page summary and the SOW with the following bounded terms we can present to your execs: 

1) Phased activation: 25% on sign, +50% at month 3, +25% at month 9. Activations require 30-day notice; acceleration allowed with 30-day notice.
2) Price-trigger remedy: if CloudVendor spot index > 18% vs baseline for a 30-day rolling window in months 0–12, Nebula may elect either: (A) a one-time credit covering incremental infra cost for the trigger window, OR (B) to de-activate up to 30% of the committed but inactive pool. Not both.
3) Cap: total credits under this clause capped at 15% of year-1 committed spend.
4) Operational SLA: de-activation/activation lead time 48–72 hours; token-level export and 12 months audit log included.

We're happy to present this in your exec meeting Wednesday and walk through the exposure model Karthik prepared (see pricing_matrix.xlsx). If Nebula needs a higher cap for internal sign-off, we'll need a finance exception — Laura, can you confirm approval flow and whether a 20% cap would require VP sign-off?

Asha — if this looks good I can route the SOW for initial signatures today (DocuSign link included); otherwise tell me the point you want adjusted before Wednesday.

Thanks —
Rachel
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
